dashboards do this): above ~1600px of content area the capped column
centres itself, which spends ~50px a side on nothing before the body's
own gutter even starts.

The header's own side gutter, as a CSS length. Must match the page body
below it or the trail and the first card start on different left edges.
Defaults to 1.5rem, which dates from the header living outside the
shell's PagePanel. It renders inside PagePanel now, so that default is
added to PagePanel's own 2rem — pass `'0'` (and drop the body's `px-6`)
to let PagePanel be the single gutter instead of the third one.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom body — replaces the auto-rendered rule list.

props.name: selected
props.description: Currently selected values.

props.name: multiselect
props.description: Allow picking multiple items.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Placeholder text when no items match the search.

props.name: searchable
props.description: Show a search filter input.

props.name: cluster
props.description:
Pinned block between the brand and the scrolling nav — e.g. a global
 Search / Inbox / My-work cluster. Stays put like brand/footer.

props.name: collapsed
props.description:
Icon-rail (collapsed) mode — centres the burst over the icon instead of
 anchoring it near the left edge of a full-width row.

props.name: active
props.description: The id of the currently active tab. Bindable.

props.name: raisedEdgeIds
props.description:
Edges painted ABOVE the nodes instead of beneath them. Edges are otherwise
 drawn first, so a link between two distant nodes disappears under every
 node it passes; raising one keeps a link the operator just made visible
 across the whole canvas.

props.name: showGrid
props.description: Background grid. Off for ambient / marketing canvases.

props.name: allowNodeDrag
props.description: Node dragging. Off for passive canvases that only select + hover.

props.name: allowLinkDraw
props.description: Port-to-port link drawing. Off for read-only meshes.

props.name: edgeCurve
props.description:
'line' = straight port-to-port · 'bezier' = horizontal-eased curve ·
 'bow' = quadratic bowed perpendicular to the link, so two nodes joined by
 several links fan apart instead of overprinting.

props.name: insetLeafLabels
props.description:
For ringed leaf-icon nodes that carry a value, draw a smaller glyph and
 stack the label + value INSIDE the disc instead of below it. Used by the
 overview globe so every mode reads as a self-contained token.

props.name: unselectedDim
props.description:
How far a node unrelated to the selection is faded, 0..1.
 1 leaves the mesh untouched. Low values make selection read as isolation:
 right when the neighbours are context you are finished with, wrong when
 they are the answer to "where am I" — which is what they are on a globe
 the camera has just flown you across.

props.name: glBodies
props.description:
A GL layer is drawing the solids, so don't draw them here.
 Only the BODY is withheld. The hit proxy, caption and beacon stay, because
 they are the parts that must be pointed at, read by a screen reader, or
 laid out against other text — none of which a GPU does for free.

props.name: labelScale
props.description:
Scale the node NAME relative to everything else in the disc.
 The default sizing assumes a mesh label is a short code (`DEP·ANALYSIS`)
 sitting above a readout that is the point of the node. A layer whose
 labels ARE the content — a roadmap initiative — needs the opposite
 emphasis, and scaling it here keeps the wrap, the chord and the readout
 offsets all consistent with the new size.

props.name: typeLabels
props.description:
Print the node's TYPE above its name (`AGENTIC`, `PROXY`, …).
 That taxonomy is the mesh's own, so a layer borrowing these silhouettes
 to stand for something else — a roadmap initiative, say — would be
 labelling every node with a word that means nothing in its domain.

props.name: depthSortedParticles
props.description:
Give edge particles the same paint depth as their line. By default the
 particle stream is drawn ABOVE every node so energy is never occluded; on
 the globe that floats back-of-sphere energy over the near nodes. When set,
 base-edge particles paint behind the nodes (raised-edge particles still
 ride on top), so energy weaves through depth like the static web does.

props.name: onFacetSelect
props.type: (nodeId: string, mode: string, index: number) => void
props.description:
A fanned-out mode facet was clicked. `index` is the facet's occurrence
 among same-mode facets (0-based), for instance-precise targeting.

props.name: onNodeHover
props.type: (id: string | null, screenPos: { x: number; y: number } | null) => void
props.description:
Hover enter/leave with the cursor position in layer-local screen space,
 so a parent can float a card next to it. Null on leave.

props.name: nodes
props.description:
Logical nodes INCLUDING the hub. Positions are ignored on entry — this
 component owns them.

props.name: edges
props.description:
Edges are pure passthrough — bind them so a draft link the operator draws
 writes straight back to the caller's array (MeshStudio adds it there).

props.name: layout
props.description:
The arrangement. Bindable so the on-canvas arrangement control (see
 `layoutPicker`) can change it without a header sitting above the canvas.

props.name: hubId
props.description: Which node is the crest — the fixed centre of every layout.

props.name: camera
props.description: The <Canvas> camera handle, exposed so the caller can fly to a node.

props.name: onFacetSelect
props.type: (nodeId: string, mode: string, index: number) => void

props.name: concept
props.description: MeshStudio passthroughs.

props.name: nodeR
props.description: Default footprint radius for a node that declares none.

props.name: margin
props.description: Placement clearances (px).

props.name: laneClearance
props.description: Radial only — hold each hub→spoke line clear, up to this many spokes.

props.name: groupKeyOf
props.description: Grouping key per node for the 'grouped' layout (defaults to one group).

props.name: radiusOf
props.description:
A node's FOOTPRINT radius for placement — the room it actually occupies once
connection rings, captions and fanned facets are counted, which can exceed
the drawn disc radius (`r`). Defaults to `r`; a caller that draws rings around
nodes should pass the larger footprint so they don't overlap.

props.name: globeSensitivity
props.description: Globe tuning.

props.name: globeFrontFade
props.description:
How much a node dims between the point nearest the eye and the limb, on
 the side you can see. Small on purpose — this is atmosphere, and the
 moment it is strong enough to notice as an effect it is reading as a
 vignette instead of as distance.

props.name: globeControls
props.description:
Show the on-canvas globe controls (spin / reset / auto-rotate / zoom),
 bottom-right. Only rendered in the 'globe' layout.

props.name: layoutPicker
props.description:
Show the arrangement picker in the same on-canvas control cluster. Unlike
 the globe rows it renders in EVERY layout — otherwise leaving 'globe'
 would take the only way back with it.

props.name: autoRotateSpeed
props.description: Radians the globe advances per auto-rotate frame.

props.name: autoRotate
props.description:
Whether the globe is auto-rotating. Bindable so the on-canvas toggle and a
 caller can share the state; pass `true` to start spinning by default.

props.name: axialTilt
props.description:
Radians the spin axis tips toward the viewer, giving a planet-like tilted
 spin instead of a flat upright turn. 0 keeps the axis vertical.

props.name: insetLeafLabels
props.description:
Draw ringed leaf nodes with a smaller glyph and the label + value stacked
 inside the disc (passed through to MeshStudio).

props.name: typeLabels
props.description:
Print the node's TYPE as an eyebrow above its name (passed through to
 MeshStudio). On a mesh of infrastructure the kind of node is half the
 story; on a mesh whose labels are already real names it is the same word
 stamped on everything. Defaults on, matching MeshStudio.

props.name: tuning
props.description:
Per-canvas overrides on the studio's draw knobs, merged over DEFAULT_TUNING.
 For a caller that has to change what the canvas DRAWS from its own controls
 — a mesh big enough that per-link rings or per-link labels stop being
 legible needs to turn them off from the page, not from the demo cog.

props.name: globeIntro
props.description:
Play the orbit fly-in once when the globe layout first appears. Off by
 default; the DevCog can always replay it regardless.

props.name: globeLabel
props.description: Label for this globe in the DevCog's globe controls.

props.name: globeFill
props.description:
How much bigger than a tight fit the globe reads. 1 fits it exactly; 1.2
 makes the sphere fill 20% more of the frame. Node discs are counter-scaled
 by the same factor, so they keep the size they had at the tight fit and the
 extra room goes into the space BETWEEN them.

props.name: hudInsets
props.description:
Edges of the canvas that floating chrome (stat cards, tickers, controls)
 occupies. The globe is fitted to — and centred in — what is left, so a node
 is never placed underneath a panel. Pixels.

props.name: focusOnSelect
props.description:
Selecting a node turns the globe until that node faces the viewer.
 Off by default. An unrequested camera move is disorienting on a mesh
 where selection only means "show me the details" — it is the pairing with
 a drawer that turns it into navigation rather than the globe wandering.

props.name: focusDurationMs
props.description:
How long that turn takes, ms. Long enough to read as the globe rotating
 and not as a cut; short enough that it never feels like waiting.

props.name: focusTilt
props.description:
Radians the focused node is lifted ABOVE the middle of the disc, so a
 solid standing there is seen head-on instead of from directly overhead.
 0 centres it exactly — which is the worst view of a building there is.

props.name: focusDistance
props.description:
View distance, in globe radii, the camera closes to on focus. Lower is
 nearer. Below about 1.8 the perspective divide gets violent and the near
 limb starts to bow.

props.name: focusContext
props.description:
How much room the jib leaves around the focused node, in multiples of its
 own radius. 1 crops to the node itself; larger keeps more of the ground it
 is standing on. Too tight and the subject loses the terrain that says
 where it is — the point is a building IN a landscape, not a portrait.

props.name: focusZoomSteps
territoryDistance
props.description:
View distance, in globe radii, a flight to a TERRITORY closes to. Further
 out than `focusDistance` on purpose: the subject is a region several nodes
 across, and diving to node range crops the very grouping being shown.

props.name: territoryContext
props.description:
How much room a territory flight leaves around the region, as a multiple of
 the cap's own projected radius. Above 1 keeps the borders either side of it
 in shot, which is what makes it read as one region among several.

props.name: glPieces
props.description:
Draw the buildings with WebGL2 instead of SVG.
 Opt-in while both renderers exist. The SVG path stays the fallback for a
 browser without WebGL2 — `GlobePieces` reports that itself and draws
 nothing, so the switch is also the A/B: same scene, same camera, one
 renderer swapped, measurable with the QA cog's frame capture.

props.name: globeTerritories
props.description:
Pack the globe into TERRITORIES — one region per `groupKeyOf` key — rather
 than sowing every node evenly over the sphere. Needs `groupKeyOf`; without
 one there are no groups to divide the surface into and it is ignored.
 A grouped globe is necessarily BIGGER than an even one at the same node
 size: the empty borders between regions are surface that no node may use,
 and that space is the entire reason a region reads as a region.

props.name: territoryOf
props.description:
How to NAME and tint a territory. Returning null leaves the region unnamed
 (still clustered — just not captioned). Only consulted when
 `globeTerritories` is on.

props.name: territoryFraction
props.description:
Share of the sphere the regions may occupy between them; the rest is the
 border. Passed straight to `packSphereClusters`.

props.name: focusTerritory
props.description:
Which territory the globe currently holds in focus — the one it tints.
 Reported OUT (bindable) so a caller listing the territories can light the
 same row the globe is lighting, whether the focus came from
 `flyToTerritory` or from clicking a node that happens to live there.

props.name: territoryWallHeight
props.description:
How far a territory wall stands off the sphere, in GLOBE RADII — so it
 keeps its proportion however big the sphere packs. 0 lays it flat back on
 the surface. Bindable, and driveable live from the QA cog.

props.name: pieceLean
props.description:
How far a 3D node piece leans back toward the viewer, RADIANS.
 0 stands every piece straight up out of the sphere, which is honest and
 unreadable: a piece at the centre of the visible disc is then seen from
 directly overhead, and a house and a factory have the same roof. The lean
 is constant in camera space — see `tangentFrame` for why it must be
 constant rather than strongest where it is most needed.

props.name: terrain
props.description:
Ground under the globe. Without one the sphere is perfectly smooth, and
 anything standing on it can only ever sit ON the surface — there is
 nothing to sit IN. With one, every node rides its own elevation and a
 piece is buried to its footings in the patch beneath it.

props.name: relief
props.description:
Half-range of the terrain's elevation, in globe radii. Small: this is
 ground for the mesh to stand on, not a landscape to look at.

props.name: pieceSink
props.description:
How deep a piece sits in the ground, in node radii. Enough that the
 ground closes over its footings; more and the building sinks.

props.name: globeSurface
props.description:
Which globe you get, as ONE switch:
  · 'relief' — ground, solids standing in it, walls standing up.
  · 'flat'   — a smooth sphere, disc nodes, walls lying on the surface.
 One switch and not three, because the three are not independent: a
 building on a smooth sphere sits on nothing, and a wall standing up
 around flat markers is a fence around a diagram. Each set is coherent
 with itself, and the two are what a viewer would call two views.
 It changes only how the globe is DRAWN. The pack, the camera and the
 territories are identical in both, so switching never moves a node.

props.name: cx
props.description: Centre of the globe, in canvas coords.

props.name: radius
props.description: The sphere the nodes sit on — the same radius they were placed with.

props.name: viewDistance
props.description: Must match the projection the nodes use, or the web won't sit under them.

props.name: meridians
props.description: Lines of longitude — full great circles through both poles.

props.name: parallels
props.description:
Lines of latitude between the poles. Poles themselves are a point, not a
 circle, so they are never drawn.

props.name: surface
props.description:
How solid the globe's interior is, 0..1.
 What actually sells it as a body is that the canvas GRID stops at its
 edge — an object you can't see the floor through. So the interior is
 filled with the page background rather than tinted with the accent: a
 tint recolours the grid, it doesn't hide it.
 Not 1: the far side still has to show through, or spinning the globe
 stops being a way to find anything and the depth cues have nothing to
 act on.

props.name: terrain
props.description:
The ground, MASKED to the territories.
 The grid has to ride the same terrain the land does, or there are two
 surfaces: a wireframe sphere, and a wireframe landscape hovering over it
 with the sphere's own lines showing through from underneath. Nothing then
 looks joined, because nothing IS — the nodes stand on one and the globe
 is the other.
 A masked field makes this safe as well as right: it is exactly zero
 outside every region, so the grid stays on the sphere everywhere there is
 no land and rises only where there is. One surface, continuous, and the
 shore is where it meets itself.

props.name: relief
props.description: Height of the highest ground, in globe radii.

props.name: terrain
props.description:
The ground. A territory is not an outline on a sphere — it is a piece of
 LAND, and its floor is drawn as a contour web rising out of the surface.
 What is between territories gets no floor and no web: not sea, nothing.
 Expected to be cut to these same caps (see terrain `maskTerrain`), so the
 land falls to the surface exactly at the shore.

props.name: relief
props.description: Height of the highest ground, in globe radii.

props.name: contourInterval
props.description:
Elevation between neighbouring contour lines, in the field's own units
 (a masked terrain runs 0..1). The map's scale, and the one knob that
 decides how much ink the floor costs — halving it doubles the lines
 everywhere. Every 5th comes out as a heavier index contour.
 Set against the field's REAL range, not its nominal one. `maskTerrain`
 lifts to 0..1, but the interior of a region only reaches roughly 0.25–0.75
 — summed waves almost never peak together — so an interval chosen for the
 full range yields two or three lines and an empty-looking map.

props.name: moving
props.description:
Whether the camera is currently flying. Drops the per-frame-expensive
 ornament — see the bloom on the wall below — for as long as nobody could
 see it anyway.

props.name: value
props.description: The active layout. Bindable.

props.name: options
props.description: Options to offer. Defaults to the full MESH_LAYOUTS set.

props.name: label
props.description: Heading above the grid.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns in the option grid.

props.name: count
props.description: Badge on the button — e.g. how many filters the caller has applied.

props.name: children
props.description: Extra popover content below the arrangement picker (filters, folding…).

props.name: vendors
props.description: Third-party vendors monitored via threat feeds + the vendor agent.

props.name: vendorAgentLabel
props.description: Label for the auto-added vendor-agent node. Default 'VENDOR AGENT'.

props.name: threatFeedLabel
props.description: Label for the auto-added threat-feeds source node. Default 'THREAT FEEDS'.

props.name: seen
props.description: Telemetry counters printed over the canvas.

props.name: animate
props.description: Boot cascade + count-up on mount. Default true.

props.name: ambient
props.description: Periodic block-flares once settled. Default true.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Enables hover preview + click detail card. Default false (pure ambient).

props.name: height
props.description: CSS height of the hero.

props.name: layout
props.description:
Node arrangement. 'membrane' (default) is the native left→right trust-
gradient pipeline (world → guards → core in fixed columns). The other five
are the SAME options the agent-management mesh offers — 'grouped', 'packed',
'radial', 'fan' and 'globe' — all arranged around the protected-core crest.
Bindable, so a picker can drive it.

props.name: showLayoutPicker
props.description: Show the arrangement picker docked over the canvas (drives `layout`).

props.name: ground
props.type: { x: number; y: number; near: boolean }[]

props.name: kind
props.description: Which effect to play. `none` renders nothing.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Replay key — increment to play again. 0 = idle (nothing shown).

props.name: anchorX
props.description: Origin of point bursts. Any CSS length/percent. Default: centre.

props.name: color
props.description: Accent colour for the particles. Defaults to the theme accent.

props.name: reverse
props.description:
Play the effect backwards — particles converge instead of scattering,
sweeps run the other way. Every effect is authored as an outward burst,
so this is a pure `animation-direction` flip rather than a second set of
keyframes: the closing half of a lifecycle is the opening half in
reverse, and stays that way for free as effects are added.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Custom trigger snippet — receives `{ open }`. Defaults to the ⋮ kebab button.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the default kebab trigger.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description:
Whether picking an item closes the menu. Default true — one action, done.
Pass false for a multi-select set (`selected` on every item), where
closing after each tick makes choosing three things cost three openings.

props.name: footer
props.description:
Arbitrary content pinned below the items, under a separator — for the
one input a menu of choices cannot express (a free-text value, a link
out). Clicks inside it do not dismiss the menu. Keep it small: a menu
that grows a form is a popover wearing the wrong component.

props.name: autoDismiss
props.description:
Close the menu after a period of no hover and no focus, playing the
exit animation as the node is destroyed. Off unless asked for; see
`ACTIONS_MENU_DISMISS` for the shared defaults.
  autoDismiss                      → on, 2s, collapse
  autoDismiss={{ idleMs: 5000 }}   → on, 5s
  autoDismiss={false}              → off (the default)

props.name: ondismiss
props.description: Fired when the idle timer — not a click or Escape — closed the menu.

props.name: flourish
props.description:
Selection flourish played on the default kebab when it opens the menu.
Omit to follow the user's "Nav selection effect" theme setting, which is
the point — one preference drives the side nav and the kebabs alike.
Pass `'none'` to opt this menu out regardless of the setting.
Only applies to the built-in trigger: a custom `trigger` snippet is the
caller's markup, so its flourish is the caller's to render.

props.name: container
props.description: The frame — the thing being broken out of. Establishes the box.

props.name: overlay
props.description: The art that escapes. Centred on the container.

props.name: breakout
props.description: 0–1. How far the overlay breaks out. 0 leaves it contained.

props.name: grow
props.description: Overlay scale at breakout 1. 1.45 clears a shield-shaped container.

props.name: lift
props.description: Upward shift, % of container height, at breakout 1.

props.name: pad
props.description: Reserve flow space for the overhang.

props.name: originX
props.description:
Fractional origin the overlay grows about — 0.5/0.5 is its centre.
 Drop it below centre to push the growth upward.

props.name: pressed
props.description:
Marks a `pill` as the active choice — fills it with `tone` and sets
aria-pressed, so a set of pills reads as a toggle group.

props.name: href
props.description: When set, renders as `<a>`; otherwise renders as `<button>`.

props.name: target
props.description: Anchor target — forwarded to `<a>` only.

props.name: full
props.description: Stretches the button to fill its container.

props.name: form
props.description: Associates the button with a form by id — forwarded to `<button form>`.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Neither on nor off — for a box standing in for a partly-selected set.

props.name: outline
props.description: Wraps the chip in an animated RGB conic-gradient outline.

props.name: value
props.description: Current set of selected chip values.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Suggestions shown in the dropdown (filtered by query).

props.name: onquery
props.description:
Fires on every query change (and on open, with ''). Lets the host compute
live results (e.g. cross-entity search) and feed them back via `commands`.

props.name: externalFilter
props.description:
Host owns filtering: when true, `commands` is rendered verbatim (no internal
`label.includes` pass) so the host can return ranked/fuzzy results. Pair with
`onquery`. Default false keeps the built-in substring filter.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a subtle loading row (e.g. while a manifest/fetch is in flight).

props.name: action
props.description: Optional action (e.g. a danger Button) placed at the right end.

props.name: edge
props.description: Which edge the toolbar docks against.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: The docked rail. When omitted, the card renders content only.

props.name: class
props.description: Extra classes on the outer card (e.g. sizing / max-width).

props.name: contentClass
props.description: Classes for the content wrapper (padding, inner layout).

props.name: sub
props.description: Optional sub-text shown below the message.

props.name: variant
props.description: `'inline'` — centered text in a fixed-height area (default). `'card'` — bordered rounded box.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon snippet rendered above the message.

props.name: formats
props.description: Formats to include. Defaults to all four.

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the trigger icon (default: download).

props.name: label
props.description: Tooltip / aria-label for the trigger button.

props.name: placeholder
props.default: 'Drag & drop, paste, or click to browse'

props.name: error
props.description: Inline error message — shows below the field with red styling.

props.name: showOptional
props.description: Render a muted "(optional)" tag after the label when not required.

props.name: id
props.description: Should match the id on the child input for label association.

props.name: speed
props.description: Animation speed in seconds per revolution. Default 5s.

props.name: status
props.description: Visual state — drives border + focus color.

props.name: min
props.description: Numeric constraints — forwarded to `<input>`; `type="number"` only.

props.name: label
props.description: Override the rendered label. Defaults to the status keyword.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Border around the text label (full pill). Set false for plain text only.

props.name: filled
props.description: Renders a filled accent pill (e.g. status-page "operational"). Overrides `bordered`.

props.name: dot
props.description: Show a leading status dot.

props.name: glow
props.description: Show a glow shadow. Default true for live dashboards, set false for static lists.

props.name: pulse
props.description: Pulse animation for live state.

props.name: chip
props.description: Console-chip styling: cut-corner clip-path, sharp aesthetic. Default is rounded marketing tile.

props.name: content
props.description: Plain text label. Ignored when `tip` snippet is provided.

props.name: placement
props.description: Which side of the trigger to attach to.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds to wait before showing.

props.name: tip
props.description: Rich tooltip body — overrides `content` when provided.

props.name: children
props.description: The trigger element.

props.name: initials
props.description: Single letter or short initials displayed in the avatar box.

props.name: tag
props.description: Eyebrow label — e.g. "ENG · 01". In rich mode, `docId` overrides this.

props.name: title
props.description: Main card title

props.name: meta
props.description: Footer metadata line — e.g. "DRAFT · 2026-05-13" (simple mode only)

props.name: variant
props.description: Accent color for the left edge bar, TR corner, and tag text

props.name: status
props.description: Status controls the dot color in the meta row. Rich mode accepts any string.

props.name: metaSlot
props.description: Optional override of the meta area (simple mode)

props.name: href
props.description: When set, the card renders as an anchor to this href.

props.name: icon
props.description: SVG path `d` for the header glyph — presence enables rich layout.

props.name: docId
props.description: Document identifier shown in the header (defaults to `tag`).

props.name: version
props.description: Version badge, rendered as `v{version}`.

props.name: classification
props.description: Classification label, shown at the top-right.

props.name: tags
props.description: Tag chips; overflow past `maxTags` collapses into a `+N` chip.

props.name: maxTags
props.description: Maximum tag chips before the `+N` overflow chip. Default 4.

props.name: authors
props.description: Author avatars (initials). First 3 are shown.

props.name: authorText
props.description: Fallback author byline when `authors` is empty.

props.name: updated
props.description: Date suffix appended to the status text (rich mode).

props.name: shape
props.description: `'bracket'` (default) — L-bracket corners. `'cut-corner'` — diagonal clip + accent bars.

props.name: onclick
props.description: When set, renders as `<button>` so the whole card is interactive.

props.name: children
props.description: The art to treat.

props.name: type
props.description: Which treatment.

props.name: host
props.description: How the effect is hosted — see the note above.

props.name: enabled
props.description:
Turn the effect off without unmounting the art, so a toggle does not
 remount whatever is inside.

props.name: bleed
props.description: Filter region bleed, % of the content box per side. Raise if clipped.

props.name: title
props.description:
Accessible name. Given one, the <svg> is exposed as an image; without
 one it is hidden from assistive tech, which is right for decoration.

props.name: risk
props.description: The risk being edited. Omit (or pass null) to file a new one.

props.name: owners
props.description: Assignable owners for the tracking card. Empty leaves the risk unassigned.

props.name: dataClasses
props.description:
The org's data-class policy — tier and summary per class, as edited in
Org Settings. Defaults to the platform classes so the component still
renders standalone, but a host that has the org's guidance should pass
it: the tier drives the colour AND the suggested impact, so showing
platform defaults to an org that has retiered a class is a wrong answer.

props.name: onReview
props.description:
Stamps the review date on an existing risk (POST /risks/:id/review).
Omit and the Review step reports the due date without offering to close
it out — a new risk has nothing to stamp until it has been filed.

props.name: onReady
props.description: Hands the commit controls up so the page's action strip can drive them.

props.name: onEdit
props.description: Open the editor page for an existing risk — the register does not edit in place.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: Open the editor page for a new risk.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Rows per page. Omit to size the page to whatever fits the viewport.

props.name: onReady
props.description: Hands the register's open actions up so a page's own toolbar can drive them.

props.name: section
props.description: Which group to render. The rail decides; this component only draws.

props.name: display
props.default:
$bindable({
			lanes: true,
			columns: true,
			deps: true,
			meta: true,
			grid: true,
			focus: false,
		})

props.name: density
props.description:
Scales column width and card size together. One knob, because scaling
 them independently is how a roadmap ends up with cards that no longer
 fit their columns.

props.name: showSpan
props.description:
Only the timeline reads `span`, so the control is only offered there — a
 slider that silently does nothing is worse than no slider.

props.name: showAppearance
props.description:
Icon, colour and silhouette. Only the mesh-drawn views render them, so
 the section is hidden in the card views rather than offering settings
 that quietly do nothing.

props.name: filter
props.description:
Narrows what is laid out. Applied BEFORE layout, so a filtered roadmap
 re-packs tight instead of leaving holes.

props.name: focus
props.description:
Dim everything outside the selected item's dependency chain. The main
 exploration affordance — a 20-card roadmap has too many lines to read
 until you can ask it about one thing.

props.name: showMeta
props.description:
Owner, effort and tag chrome on each card. Off gives clean title-only
 cards, which is usually what a slide wants.

props.name: onChange
props.description: An item was re-assigned or pinned by dragging.

props.name: onLayout
props.description:
Fires whenever the layout re-solves — the page needs the bounds for
 fit-to-view and for framing an export.

props.name: svgEl
props.description: The layer's own <svg>, for export.

props.name: showShells
props.description: Horizon rings and the hub.

props.name: showBand
props.description: The strip itself — edge curve plus cross-rungs.

props.name: band
props.description: Half-width of the band, world units.

props.name: showRibbon
props.description:
The ribbon itself. Off leaves the stages floating, which is occasionally
 what a busy slide wants.

props.name: showNumbers
props.description: Stage numbers under each node.

props.name: perRow
props.description: Stages per row before the ribbon folds back.

props.name: rowGap
props.description:
Vertical spacing between rows — and so also the U-turn's diameter, since
 the fold is a semicircle on that chord.

props.name: perRow
props.description:
Stages per row before the ribbon folds. Ribbon only — a Möbius strip has
 no rows, so the control is hidden there rather than disabled.

props.name: rowGap
props.description: Vertical spacing between rows, and so also the U-turn's diameter.

props.name: shape
props.description: Which sequence view is showing — decides which knobs are on offer.

props.name: present
props.description: Chrome off, camera fitted — what you screenshot.

props.name: onPick
onPreview
props.type: (sel: { channel?: string; burst?: string; to?: unknown } | null) => void
props.description: Null clears the preview.

props.name: selectedId
props.description: Raw selection id — the hub selects but resolves to no scene object.

props.name: onMove
props.type: (id: string, x: number, y: number) => void

props.name: globePose
props.type: { yaw: number; pitch: number; viewDistance: number } | null

props.name: onSelect
props.description:
Selection is REPORTED, never bound. MeshStudio and SceneStage both own a
 local notion of it; binding here let the child update its copy while the
 parent never heard, so clicking the canvas selected nothing.

props.name: onPin
props.type: (id: string, x: number, y: number) => void

props.name: onMoveComponent
props.type: (id: string, x: number, y: number) => void

props.name: onUserCamera
props.description: The operator took the camera — the beat camera should stand down.

props.name: onDropComponent
props.type: (componentId: string, x: number, y: number) => void

props.name: children
props.description: Overlaid ON the stage, above the canvas — captions and the like.
